summary: Rushing Mountain (Big Hill) lookout, Tuolumne County: tower erected by the state with county funds in 1931; Cal Fire TCU; NHLR-registered 2019; not open to the public.

facts.design: Steel Aermotor-built tower with a glass cab; CCC-built residence and garage, house based on the Forest Service BC-201 plan with the front entry altered
facts.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection - Tuolumne-Calaveras Unit (Cal Fire TCU)

access.note: NHLR: the site is not open to the public and is 2 miles from a paved road

visit.trail_note: NHLR: site not open to the public; 2 miles from paved road.

events.note: NHLR: Rushing Mountain became a fire detection site in 1921
NHLR gives 1931 as the build year; Peakbagging says probably built in 1931. The 1931 newspaper items describe the tower going up in April and May, paid for by Tuolumne and Stanislaus counties
A May 14, 1931 item says Ed Tinney of Keystone is to be assigned as watchman; the June 26, 1931 Modesto News-Herald names Edward H. Tinnen as lookout on the newly constructed tower
July 8, 1936 Oakland Tribune item names Frank Tinney as lookout at Rushing Mountain
NHLR: the east end has been enlarged to the full 19-foot width; this may have been done in 1970, when the facilities were rented out on a year-round basis
2011 visit: the residence appeared to have been an FM radio transmitter site and is now abandoned. The tower is noted only as looking about the same condition, with no comparison point given

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives no height. A 1931 newspaper item says forty feet, another says thirty feet, and Peakbagging (2011) says 35 feet. No height is recorded.
NHLR gives 1,517 ft (462 m); Peakbagging gives 1,525 ft. The record keeps the NHLR figure.

A 1930 report places the proposed site at the top of a hill on the W.H. Rushing ranch west of Keystone; 1931 items place the tower near Oakdale and between Knights Ferry and Keystone. The county is consistent; the exact spot is not reconciled.
Newspapers name Ed Tinney, Edward H. Tinnen and Frank Tinney as lookouts in 1931 and 1936. Whether these are the same people or different staff is not reconciled.
A February 26, 1931 item says the Forest Service will maintain the lookout during the danger season; a May 14, 1931 item says the state will maintain it. Not reconciled.

notes_for_editor: The brief's record is correct on the 1931 build year and the NHLR elevation. Access was 'unknown' but NHLR says the site is not open to the public. Heights disagree across sources (30, 35, 40 ft), so none is recorded. Staffing is from a 2007-era photo page and undated text; no current staffing source was read. The 1970 rental and enlargement are hedged in NHLR. Peakbagging calls this lookout 'Big Hill', but the Eldorado National Forest has a separate Big Hill Lookout; do not conflate the two. Newspaper quotes come through Forest Lookouts; the original newspaper pages were not read.
